newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PFI says will exceed NZ$7 mln year profit.
newsitem.headline: PFI says will exceed NZ$7 mln year profit.

text.p: Property for Industry said on Thursday it expected its full year profit for the 1997 year to exceed NZ$7 million.
The company also said it had approximately NZ$30 million to invest, adding to its current investment portfolio worth around NZ$120 million and bringing it to full investment.
Earlier, the comppany reported a profit for the year to December 31, 1996, of NZ$5.29 million ($5.19 million in 1995), and declared a dividend of 3.075 NZ cents per share.
PFI said it had 27 tenants, with an average rental return on warehouse properties of $62/square metre and on new construction rentals of $75-85/square metre.
PFI said it was achieving 5.0-8.0 percent rental growth on reviews and a yield on valuation of 10.5 percent.
General Manager David Jans said it was the company's view that it would achieve a long-term sustainable yield of nine to 10 percent gross before tax.
While the company had reached critical mass, it was looking for further investment opportunities in industrial property that offered promising returns. Profits were also expected to grow.
"We'll exceed $7 million (profit for the full year)," chairman Allan Lockie told journalists after the result announcement.
PFI noted that its 1996 year profit included $662,000 rights issue expenses and if these were excluded, its profit was $5.949 million.
Jans said PFI's portfolio was currently worth around $120 million and the company had about $30 million left to take it to a fully invested position, which it anticipated doing during this year.
"Thirty million dollars would take us to a fully invested position. We won't go there as a matter of course, we will go there dependent on the opportunities that emerge over the year," Jans said.
"At this stage we certainly do have a host of opportunities in front of us."
